rationale: The literature characterizes KDM2B-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621474) as exhibiting core neurodevelopmental delay and high-frequency congenital heart defects (~78%), with renal and ocular abnormalities occurring as variable/intermediate manifestations. Ocular phenotypes including structural eye anomalies (coloboma/microphthalmia spectrum), refractive errors (e.g., myopic astigmatism in 3/3 patients in Gomes et al.), and renal anomalies such as solitary kidney and unilateral renal agenesis (reported in Gomes et al. and Ceroni et al.) occur in an intermediate/variable subset of affected individuals with CxxC domain variants.

evidence.text: In a clinical study of 19 individuals with KDM2B CxxC domain variants, congenital heart defects were identified in up to 78% of individuals, whereas ophthalmological and urogenital anomalies were documented as common but variable co-occurring anomalies alongside musculoskeletal and neurodevelopmental features.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals, with additional common findings including musculoskeletal, ophthalmological, and urogenital anomalies, as well as behavioral challenges and feeding difficulties.

evidence.text: In a cohort of three pediatric patients with heterozygous variants in the CxxC domain of KDM2B, all three (3/3) presented with ocular abnormalities specifically characterized as myopic astigmatism, while one patient (1/3) had a structural renal malformation (solitary kidney / unilateral renal agenesis).

source.title: KDM2B‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case‐Series Supporting the CxxC Domain Phenotype With Emphasis on Ocular and Dermatologic Features
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Patient 1 is a 2-year-old boy with developmental delay, solitary kidney, atrial septal defect, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 2 is a 2-year-old girl with global developmental delay, hip dysplasia, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 3 is a 5-year-old girl with autism, developmental delay, atrial septal defect, and ventricular septal defect, hypertrichosis, atopic dermatitis, and myopic astigmatism.

evidence.text: Screening of 706 families presenting with developmental eye defects identified two individuals carrying heterozygous KDM2B CxxC domain variants; both presented with complex structural eye anomalies accompanied by variable cardiac and renal malformations.

source.title: Variants in the CxxC domain of the epigenetic regulator KDM2B support its role in developmental eye anomalies
source.quote: Both individuals exhibited complex structural eye defects, with neurodevelopmental, cardiac and renal anomalies variably present. These cases strengthen the association between KDM2B-CxxC variants and eye, kidney and heart malformations

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of structural ocular anomalies versus isolated refractive errors across the combined global cohort of KDM2B variants?
new_directions.rationale: Gomes et al. highlight mild ocular manifestations like myopic astigmatism in 100% of their small series, whereas Ceroni et al. ascertain complex structural anomalies, suggesting ascertainment bias across specialized ophthalmology vs general genetics cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: Do CxxC domain missense variants specifically enrich for renal and ocular anomalies compared to loss-of-function or JmjC domain variants?
new_directions.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. observed genotype-phenotype divergence between CxxC domain variants (which confer a distinct episignature and penetrant syndromic presentation) and haploinsufficiency or non-CxxC variants which show incomplete penetrance.
